evidence_type: direct assay (reconstituted complex, pulldown) + crystal structure
stance: supports (CH domain, IFT80 partner) / refutes (tubulin binding)
claim_tested: Does the IFT38 CH domain bind tubulin, and which IFT-B2 subunit does it bind?
key_finding: Of the three CH-domain IFT-B2 subunits (IFT38, IFT54, IFT57) only IFT54 binds alpha-beta-tubulin; the IFT38 CH domain mediates the interaction with IFT80. IFT54 CH crystal structures show tubulin binding via basic surface residues.
context: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii recombinant proteins, in vitro
confidence: High for the biochemistry. Limitation: algal orthologues, not C. elegans; no DYF-3 protein tested.

claim_tested: Is CLUAP1/IFT38 an integral IFT-B2 subunit whose binding to other IFT-B subunits is required for function?
key_finding: Cluap1/IFT38 is an integral component of the IFT-B peripheral subcomplex; a ciliogenesis defect of Cluap1-deficient MEFs was rescued by wild-type but not by a mutant Cluap1 lacking binding ability to other IFT-B components.
context: Human HEK293T expression, mouse embryonic fibroblasts
confidence: High for mammalian orthologue. Limitation: overexpression-based interaction assay; binding-deficient mutant not residue-mapped onto DYF-3 here.

citation: PDB 8BD7 / PMID:36593313 (Lacey 2023, Nat Struct Mol Biol)
evidence_type: structural (in situ cryo-ET at 9.9 A + AlphaFold2 model) re-analysed computationally here
claim_tested: Which IFT-B subunits contact IFT38 in an IFT train?
key_finding: Computed heavy-atom contacts (8 A): IFT57 695 residue pairs (IFT38 res 71-81, 119-291), IFT20 212 (11-17, 46, 76-78, 101-154), IFT52 160 (246-273, 284-299), IFT80 140 (2-15, 20-29, 90-105), IFT54 138 (106-143), IFT88 118 (251-304). IFT80 contacts fall in the CH-like domain; IFT57 contacts are mostly coiled coil.
context: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii cilia, in situ anterograde train, two independent repeats in the deposited model
confidence: Moderate. The map is 9.9 A, so side-chain-level interfaces are AlphaFold2-derived predictions docked into density, not resolved contacts.

citation: This work (AlphaFold DB AF-Q6I6D4-F1 v6; PDB 5FMT, 5FMU, 4LVP, 1QAG, 1PA7)
stance: supports (CH fold) / qualifies (fold is uninformative about ligand)
claim_tested: Does DYF-3 retain a CH fold?
key_finding: DYF-3 residues 1-115 give TM 0.599 vs CrIFT54 CH (5FMT), 0.613 vs MmIFT54 CH (5FMU), 0.595 vs IFT81 CH (4LVP), 0.614 vs utrophin CH1 (1QAG), 0.525 vs EB1 CH (1PA7), 0.659 vs the CrIFT38 N-domain in 8BD7. Negative control DYF-3 160-275 vs utrophin CH1 gives TM 0.102.
context: C. elegans DYF-3 predicted model (pLDDT 90-95 over res 1-300)
confidence: Moderate-high for fold assignment (all TM > 0.5). Limitation: prediction only; no experimental DYF-3 structure exists.

claim_tested: Is the CH-like domain and its IFT80-contacting surface under selective constraint?
key_finding: Mean per-residue identity: CH-like 1-115 = 52.7%, linker = 33.6%, coiled coil = 40.5%, acidic tail = 36.2%. 26 of the 35 positions >=90% identical lie in 1-115. IFT80-contact residues 59.8% vs 44.2% background (Mann-Whitney one-sided p = 0.0060); no other modelled interface exceeds background. PF10234 recovered in 18 ciliated lineages and absent from S. cerevisiae, A. thaliana, D. discoideum and P. falciparum.
confidence: Moderate. Within the CH domain alone the IFT80 patch is not significantly more conserved than other CH residues (p = 0.135), so most of the signal is domain-wide constraint.

citation: This work (surface charge of 5 CH domains)
claim_tested: Does DYF-3 have the basic surface associated with CH-domain tubulin binding?
key_finding: Net exposed charge (K+R minus D+E): DYF-3 1-115 = +4, human CLUAP1 = 0, Cr IFT38 = -2, Cr IFT54 CH = +1, Mm IFT54 CH = +6. Mouse IFT54 CH is the most basic (32.4% exposed K/R) but Chlamydomonas IFT54 CH is not, so basicity does not cleanly separate binders from non-binders.
confidence: Low. n = 5 domains, crude CA-neighbour burial proxy, no statistical test.

claim_tested: What does dyf-3 do in C. elegans and what isoforms does it make?
key_finding: dyf-3 mutants have stunted sensory cilia and dye-filling defects; dyf-3::gfp is expressed in 26 chemosensory neurons and acts cell-autonomously; the gene encodes three proteins with different N-termini, the largest 404 aa.
confidence: High for phenotype and expression. The three-isoform structure means a CH-domain-dependent claim may not apply to isoform 3 (res 74-404).

claim_tested: Can worm IFT proteins be assigned to physical modules from transport behaviour?
key_finding: IFT proteins were grouped into IFT-A, IFT-B and BBS modules from motility and mutant phenotypes, with the explicit caveat that binding assays would be required to confirm direct physical interactions.
context: C. elegans amphid and phasmid neurons, in vivo imaging
confidence: High for module membership, explicitly not evidence of direct binding.

claim_tested: Is there experimental C. elegans interaction evidence for DYF-3 with IFT-B subunits?
key_finding: Only 6 IntAct entries for dyf-3, all Y2H from two large screens: osm-12/BBS-7, gei-4, eif-3.K, Q18603, YW12. No che-2/IFT80, che-13/IFT57, dyf-11/IFT54, osm-6/IFT52, osm-5/IFT88 or IFT20.
confidence: High that the data are absent. Y2H screens are incomplete, so absence is weak negative evidence.

claim_tested: What is already annotated on dyf-3?
key_finding: MF is GO:0003674 with ND (nothing asserted). CC includes GO:0030992 IFT particle B (IBA, ComplexPortal NAS), GO:0005929 cilium, GO:0005815 MTOC (IBA only) and four IDA neuronal CC terms. BP includes GO:0060271 cilium assembly (IDA) and GO:0042073 intraciliary transport (NAS).
confidence: High. Any MF term would be a new annotation.
